title: Revit model file naming resolution
test_intent: Determine whether a Revit model filename can be constructed or validated from the canonical S4 container syntax plus governed or project-approved token values without inventing abbreviations, token order, delimiters, mutable identity dimensions or placeholders.

applicability.applies_when: A native Revit model file is being named, renamed, created, registered or validated as an information container.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The tested item is not a Revit model file/information container.

required_evidence: applicable controlled vocabularies or project-approved code sets
project source for project code, originator, volume/system, level/location and sequence values
approved exception or platform mapping where applicable

result_logic.pass: The filename conforms to the canonical seven-token root identity and every token value is traceable to a governed vocabulary or project-approved source; any platform-specific label preserves the canonical identity mapping.
result_logic.fail: The filename violates the available canonical syntax, uses an unauthorized token order/delimiter, embeds mutable status/revision as root identity, or uses invented/unapproved token values where governed values are available.
result_logic.not_applicable: The tested item is not a Revit model file/information container.
result_logic.indeterminate: The canonical syntax is known but one or more required project token values or applicable controlled vocabularies are unavailable or unresolved.

provenance.migration_note: Closes the Revit model-file routing/conformance gap while preserving project-instance code authority. Missing project codes remain indeterminate rather than being invented.
